tests 18, pass 18, fail 0, skipped 0, todo 0. The io fixture now carries a working deleteRef, matching githubIo, so the lease release actually happens and the idempotency assertion is no longer vacuous. Against the pre-fix script (git stash of scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs) the same fixture runs pass 16, fail 2: 'recording is create-only, bound to the assignment parent, and idempotent' and 'an existing artifact is validated against its own findings comment, not this round's (#2464)' both fail with 'reviewer does not hold the exact active lease; late or conflicting verdict refused' -- issue #2710 exactly.

assumptions_resolved: A recorded verdict now releases the lease it was recorded against. A tuple-keyed v2 lease is never drawn again, so before this change nothing reclaimed it and refs/db-review-active-v2/* grew without bound until the listing ceiling refused every draw, release, replacement, exclusion and capacity report.

The release is best-effort by design: it is compare-and-swap where the io offers one, and it never throws, because a failed release must not void a durable verdict artifact whose digest is computed over the findings comment.

A determinate listing refusal (row ceiling or a newly paginated namespace) is now marked on the error and re-raised with its own text; transient failures still fail open. No budget, ceiling or guard was widened or relaxed.
The capacity report and cutover activation read the assignment-keyed view, so one provider holding two live jobs is two rows and two backfilled leases rather than one.
No database access or mutation occurred.

#2710. The standing verdict artifact is read before the exact-lease gate, so recording stays idempotent after the verdict has handed its own lease back. The artifact's assignment_sha binding is still enforced by validateVerdictArtifact, so a late or conflicting verdict is refused unchanged, and a request with no standing artifact still meets the lease gate.

The lease a recorded verdict hands back no longer falls back to the provider-keyed legacy ref when neither name holds it, so the release cannot aim at a ref a live sibling job for the same provider is holding.
